settings.aiDesc: Configure an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (OpenAI / DeepSeek / Kimi / Qwen / SiliconFlow, etc.). Keys are stored locally only (DPAPI encrypted); requests go through the native proxy to avoid CORS.
settings.aiReason: reasoning_effort (for reasoning models like GPT-5; higher is slower but more accurate)
settings.densityDesc: Compact keeps high information density; Comfort enlarges spacing and line height. Applies immediately after saving.
settings.navModulesDesc: Choose which modules appear in the sidebar. Hidden modules stay reachable via Global Search (Ctrl+K). Keep at least one. Applies immediately after saving.
settings.autostartDesc: When enabled, ToolCove starts automatically after Windows sign-in. With the tray icon resident, daily backups are never missed.
settings.langDesc: Switch the interface language. Applies immediately after saving, no restart needed.
settings.backupDesc: Package all module data (including settings) and attached images into a zip. Restore validates the backup and keeps a safety copy of current data, then restarts the app. A daily automatic backup also runs on first launch (keeps the latest 7).
settings.restoreConfirmMsg: Restoring replaces all current data with the backup and keeps a pre-restore safety copy. Unsaved page edits will be lost, and the app restarts after success. Continue?
settings.updateDesc: Check for new versions from GitHub Releases. One-click download, install and restart; local data is not affected. Also checked automatically on launch.

prompt.extractFieldBool: (boolean true/false; checked/yes in the image means true, fill false when uncertain)
prompt.extractFieldEnum: (must be one of: {values}; leave empty when uncertain)
prompt.extractGroupLine: - {key} ({title}): array, each element represents one row of the table, fields:
prompt.extractGroupsHead: You are an information extraction assistant. The user's screenshots may contain [one or more] tables listed below. First determine which tables actually appear in the images, then extract every data row of each table into a JSON object. Output strictly one single JSON object whose keys are table names and values are row arrays; return an empty array [] for tables not present in the images. Do not output any explanation, prefixes, suffixes or code fences. Table definitions:
prompt.extractGroupsTail: Requirements: extract only data rows that truly exist in the images, never fabricate; header rows and placeholder rows (e.g. 'no data yet') are not data rows; fill an empty string for unrecognized fields (false for boolean fields). Table data may not appear as regular tables: if the images contain merged cells or free text paragraphs of remarks/notes whose content clearly maps to a table's fields (e.g. mentioning a .sql script file name and an owner implies the database scripts table), split them into rows of that table as well, leave unmapped fields empty and put remaining notes into a remarks field; still never fabricate. Pay special attention to [row-spanning merged cells]: if a cell in a column visually spans multiple rows, its content applies to all those rows, so fill the same value for that field in each of those rows; strictly judge which row each column's content belongs to by the vertical boundaries of each row, and never shift content to adjacent rows.
prompt.extractSingleHead: You are an information extraction assistant. Extract information from the user's screenshots and output strictly one single JSON object,
prompt.extractManyHead: You are an information extraction assistant. The user's screenshots may contain [multiple] records (e.g. a list or table). Extract each record in the images into a JSON object and output strictly one single JSON array,
prompt.extractFieldsIntro: do not output any explanation, prefixes, suffixes or ```json code fences. Field definitions:
prompt.extractSingleTail: Requirements: the JSON keys must match the definitions above; fill an empty string "" for fields that cannot be recognized from the images; never fabricate content that does not exist in the images.
prompt.extractManyTail: Requirements: the keys of every array element must match the definitions above; extract only entries that truly exist in the images, never fabricate; fill an empty string for unrecognized fields. Pay special attention to [row-spanning merged cells]: if a cell in a column visually spans multiple rows, its content applies to all those rows, so fill the same value for that field in each of those rows; strictly judge which row each column's content belongs to by the vertical boundaries of each row, and never shift content to adjacent rows.
prompt.extractHintSingle: Extract the fields above from this screenshot and return JSON only.
prompt.extractHintMany: Extract every record in the screenshots as an array element and return a JSON array only.
prompt.extractHintGroups: Identify the tables in the screenshots and extract every row grouped by table; return a JSON object only.
prompt.snippetExtractHint: This is a screenshot containing commands/SQL/tables/config/text, possibly with multiple entries. Extract every entry that can be saved as a snippet into one record (title, category and content).
prompt.problemExtractHint: This is a screenshot of production issues/tickets/meetings/messages, possibly with multiple entries. Extract each entry into one record (issue title, type and note).
prompt.problemAnalysisIntro: You are a senior backend/full-stack engineer. Analyze the following production issue and answer entirely in English.
prompt.problemAnalysisAsk: Based on the description, please provide: 1. possible root-cause directions (ranked by likelihood), 2. investigation steps (logs, SQL, API verification), 3. fix suggestions.
